title: Metropolis found in Buenos Aires
hook: A quarter of an hour of a lost classic waited 80 years in an Argentine archive.
peek: Fritz Lang's Metropolis was cut down soon after its 1927 premiere, and the missing scenes were thought gone for good. In 2008 a worn 16mm copy in a Buenos Aires film museum turned out to hold about 25 minutes of them.
lede: Fritz Lang's Metropolis premiered in Berlin in 1927 at around two and a half hours. Within months, distributors had cut it heavily, and the full version seemed to vanish. For decades, restorers worked from shortened prints and written notes. Then in 2008, a scratched 16mm copy in the Museo del Cine in Buenos Aires turned out to contain about 25 minutes of the missing footage.

bullets.text: An Argentine distributor brought a long version of the film to Buenos Aires in 1928. It passed through a private collection and on to the museum, where a 16mm copy was made from it decades later. The original print did not survive.

The film historian Fernando Peña had heard years earlier that someone had watched an unusually long Metropolis in Buenos Aires. In 2008 he and the museum's director, Paula Félix-Didier, checked the reel and found the scenes everyone had given up on.

The restored film, now close to Lang's original, premiered at the Berlin Film Festival in 2010. It was shown in a theatre and on a big outdoor screen at the Brandenburg Gate on the same night, with a live orchestra playing the original score.

The recovered footage was too worn to match the rest, so restorers left its scratches and darker frame visible. Viewers can see exactly which moments came back from Argentina. A few minutes are still missing.
